data.outcome_summary: The OECD PISA 2022 factsheet for Georgia summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably comparing 2012, 2015, 2018, and 2022). It reports that average 2022 scores were about the same as in 2018 across the three domains, and that the gap between the top and bottom deciles of performance did not change significantly from 2018 to 2022. In mathematics, 34% of students reached at least Level 2 proficiency (below the OECD average of 69%), while only 1% were top performers (Level 5 or 6). In reading and science, shares reaching Level 2 or higher were 33% and 35%, respectively, with very small proportions at Level 5 or 6. The factsheet also highlights within-country divides by socio-economic status and gender, and provides contextual indicators on belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences, with a caution that only 60% of students reached the COVID closure section.
